name: Rank Math
summary: WordPress SEO plugin with schema, on-page analysis and rank tracking.
best_for: WordPress site owners who want a powerful, feature-rich SEO plugin: the free version alone beats most paid rivals
skip_if: your SEO needs are basic and the free version covers them: there's no rush to PRO until you need tracking or Content AI
honest_knock: The free version is so generous that many sites never need to upgrade: PRO mainly earns its keep once you want built-in rank tracking, Content AI credits or to manage many sites. Don't pay until you hit those.

pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-10-16 on rankmath.com/pricing with its FAQ; first read 2026-08-26) Pro is €7.99 a month, Business €24.99 and Agency €54.99, each billed annually and excluding VAT, renewing at €8.99, €27.99 and €64.99 a month plus taxes; the higher figure is the renewal rate, not a comparison price. Pro covers unlimited personal sites and 500 keywords; Business 100 client sites and 10,000 keywords; Agency 500 sites and 50,000. The 30-day refund policy covers new purchases only, not renewals, and the 15-day Content AI trial that comes with each plan turns into a paid plan unless you cancel it before it ends. The euros are not a European quirk of our reading: we checked from a US connection and the storefront still priced in euros, so an American pays in euros too and carries whatever their card charges to convert.

sessions.what: Our AI assistant ran the test on 22 November 2026 in WordPress Playground, a temporary WordPress site that runs in the browser, with the free Rank Math plugin from WordPress.org and the interface in English. We went through the setup wizard without a Rank Math account, wrote a short test post, set a focus keyword, SEO title and meta description, looked at the schema options and read the page head the plugin produced. The post was published less than 4 minutes after we started. We paid nothing and opened the Pro checkout only to read the price.
findings: Setup: the wizard has six steps. The first asks you to connect a free Rank Math account and has a Skip Step button. The Analytics step, which covers Search Console, Google Analytics and keyword rank tracking, also needs that account, so we skipped it. Usage tracking was off by default.

On-page checks: the score went from 4 to 54 out of 100 when we entered the focus keyword cold brew coffee, and to 58 after we set our own title and description. The free version listed Basic SEO, Additional, Title Readability and Content Readability checks; the Fix with AI buttons lead to Content AI.

Schema: Article was applied by default. The free Schema Generator offered 13 types, including Product, Recipe, Event and Video. FAQ, HowTo, Dataset, Fact Check, Movie and Podcast Episode were marked PRO, and the panel said more than one schema per post needs Pro.

Output: after we switched on Headless CMS Support in the settings, the plugin's getHead endpoint returned our meta description, robots, canonical, Open Graph and Twitter tags, and BlogPosting schema with our title as headline.

Checkout: on 22 November 2026, in the Black Friday sale, Pro was EUR 4.99 a month billed yearly, renewing at EUR 8.99, for unlimited personal websites, and Business was EUR 14.99 for client websites. The FastSpring checkout for Pro showed EUR 72.45 for the year including 21% Dutch VAT, asked for an email and a card or PayPal, and needed no account. We did not pay.
